findings.title: All-groups VIEW is treated as permission to manage groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true if hasPermission finds either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup authorizes group creation with requireManage(), which calls this method, and any other caller of canManage()/requireManage() treats it as a write check. A fine-grained admin granted only view access to groups can therefore create top-level groups. That contradicts canManage(GroupModel) in the same class, which correctly requires only MANAGE, and contradicts V1, which only checks the manage-users role. The new javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage repeats the same mistake by documenting VIEW as sufficient. canManage() must require the MANAGE scope only.

findings.title: Group-scoped user search and counts use authorization resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is what UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to the user store (session attribute UserModel.GROUPS, and getUsersCount) so that an admin who cannot view all users only sees members of groups they may view. The callback passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission and stores that same value. hasPermission treats the argument as a group id and looks it up with resourceStore.findByName, but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource stores the group id as the resource name and the authorization store assigns a different resource id. The lookup therefore misses. findByType(GROUPS) also cannot see per-group resources, because getOrCreateResource never calls setType, so only the type resource named "Groups" (if present) is visited. The set ends up empty or filled with authorization UUIDs. User search pagination then either is not restricted to the permitted groups or is restricted to ids that match no membership, and the count API returns 0 or a count for a non-existent group. Return the group id (resource name), skip the type resource, and persist instance resources with type Groups.

findings.title: Group deletion throws when FGAP V2 is enabled
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (as do the other GroupPermissionManagement methods). AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and therefore GroupPermissionsV2, whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. With both features on, which is the normal combination if V1 is a default feature and V2 is enabled for this work, realm.removeGroup and the admin delete-group API fail with that exception and the group is not removed. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all, so the V2 authorization resource named by the group id is never deleted and remains orphaned on the admin-permissions client. Group removal needs a V2 cleanup path; the V1 listener must not call the throwing methods while V2 is active.

findings.title: A per-group permission resource hides all-groups grants
findings.body: hasPermission looks up the per-group resource by name and, if it exists, evaluates only that resource. The all-groups resource is used only when no per-group resource exists. Creating any permission on a group (including one for a different administrator) creates that resource, after which an admin who holds VIEW or MANAGE on all groups is denied for that group because their all-groups policy is never evaluated. canView, canManage, canViewMembers, canManageMembers, and canManageMembership all go through this helper. GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups no longer short-circuit on global canView() and now depend entirely on canView(group), so listing is affected as well. The new tests never combine an all-groups grant with a specific grant for another user. Evaluation has to combine the instance resource and the resource-type resource under the schema decision strategy; preferring the instance resource drops legitimate grants and also drops all-groups denies when only the instance is evaluated.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain the Groups schema
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and no other path creates the Groups resource type, the "Groups" all-resource, or the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions (the client was created when only Users and Clients existed) do not pick up this change, and turning admin permissions off and on does not help if the client row remains. Creating a group permission then fails in getScope with "Scope [view-members] does not exist". GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission also calls getResourceTypeResource, gets null, and invokes policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes() with no null check, so group admin calls from users without manage-users/view-users become 500s instead of a deny. Upgrade must add the missing scopes and the Groups type resource to existing admin-permissions clients, or init/getResourceTypeResource must create them lazily.

findings.title: Group permission resources have no human-readable name
findings.body: getResourceName resolves only the Users resource type ("All users" or the username) and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources created by getOrCreateResource use the group id as the name and never set a display name, and the new Groups type is not handled here. Permission listings for group policies therefore show a null name or a raw id instead of the group name or path, and there is no "All groups" label for the type resource. A missing user already throws ModelIllegalStateException; a missing group is silently unlabeled. Resolve group resources the same way users are resolved.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException when canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The implementation enforces canManageMembers, which is the manage-members scope, not manage-membership. Those are different permissions (managing the users in a group versus changing a user's group membership). An implementor or caller following the javadoc will check or document the wrong scope.

findings.title: Public group permission methods were removed and renamed
findings.body: GroupPermissionEvaluator is public. This change deletes getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) and renames getGroupsWithViewPermission() to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() with no bridge method. In-repo callers were updated, but any extension that implements the interface or calls the old methods will fail to compile or throw NoSuchMethodError at runtime. If this interface is part of the supported admin-permissions contract, keep the old methods as deprecated delegates; otherwise call the break out in the release notes.
